title: RAW UNREVIEWED: Theophrastus quince perfume: replacement batches enter a continuing carrier before decay
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. The source removes soaked flowers before spoilage and, for quince perfume, takes out each batch before inserting the next into prepared cool oil. Preserve a continuing oil carrier, successive ingredient batches and a removal deadline; longer contact is not always better.

differentiating_relation: BATCH1 contacts OIL, BATCH1 is removed before blackening, then BATCH2 is introduced. The inferred continuing carrier differs from the explicitly replaced batches, and preventing their decay protects the perfume.
complete_source_account: Kypros flowers left soaking too long decay and give the perfume a bad smell; prompt removal and squeezing are prescribed.
For quince perfume, the oil is first made astringent and is cool when fruit is added.
Each fruit batch is removed before blackening and before the next is introduced; blackening is linked to decay through soaking.
known_counterexplanation: An additive-only recipe leaves every batch in the same vessel, predicting accumulation rather than replacement. A new-oil-for-each-batch account deletes the serial enrichment relation. A longer-is-better extraction account misses the upper limit imposed by spoilage.
